H_hierarchical.evidence: The paper defines a flat five-state FSM: platoon-following, parking, waiting, de-parking, and joining; no parent or nested states are described.

G_guards_arith.evidence: Transitions depend on composed conditions such as joining if the platoon is in another lane OR the distance to the platoon is greater than the desired inter-vehicle distance; later following starts once the desired distance is achieved.

A_actions_nontrivial.evidence: States perform non-trivial control and communication actions: waiting broadcasts position/state/ID, joining increases speed to close the gap, following computes controls from predecessor position and velocity, and parking calculates and tracks a parking trajectory.

F_fault_recovery.evidence: No fault, emergency, abort, or recovery state is modeled; the paper explicitly says wrong decisions due to communication mistakes are not considered.

T1_cross_section_element.evidence: State names and high-level transitions are in Section 2.1/Figure 2, while state actions and controllers are spread across Sections 2.2, 2.3, 2.4, and validation results.

T2_implicit_domain_term.evidence: Domain terms such as platoon-following, de-parking, joining, and parking are mostly explained by explicit transition and control descriptions rather than requiring unstated domain rules.

T3_implicit_action_from_prose.evidence: Actions are narrated outside the state definition: joining reduces distance by increasing speed in Section 2.4, and parking/de-parking path generation and tracking are detailed in Section 2.3.

T4_multivar_arith_guard.evidence: The joining guard combines lane relation with distance threshold using OR: another lane OR distance greater than desired platoon spacing.

T5_composite_internal_behavior.evidence: There is no composite state with parent-level entry, during, or exit behavior.

T6_global_cross_cutting_recovery.evidence: No from-any-state fault or recovery transition is specified.

C1_speculative_dfs.evidence: No composite-state initialization or pseudo-state chain is present.

C2_expr_ir_smt.evidence: There are 1-2 meaningful composed guard patterns, especially lane relation OR distance-threshold checks, but not a large SMT-heavy guard set.

C3_forced_and_aspect.evidence: No cross-cutting forced transition over multiple substates and no parent-level during monitor is defined.

C4_abstract_action.evidence: The FSM includes abstract communication side effects such as broadcasting position/state/ID and sending merge-completion messages, though most actions are concrete vehicle-control maneuvers.

key_nl_quotes: There are five maneuvers a relocated vehicle can be in: platoon-following, parking, waiting, de-parking, and joining.
A joining process will be required if the platoon is in another lane or the distance to the platoon is more than the desired platoon inter-vehicle distance.
one_line_pitch: A flat but action-rich autonomous-vehicle relocation FSM stresses guard recovery and state-to-action attribution because transition logic and maneuver controllers are split across multiple paper sections.
rationale: This sample has no hierarchy or fault recovery, but it strongly exercises two known weak baseline dimensions: guarded transitions and non-trivial state actions. The FSM is explicit enough to build a reference model, while the actual actions are distributed across overview, controller, maneuver, and validation sections. Its composed lane-or-distance joining guard and communication/control side effects make it a strong stress-test for semantic extraction rather than syntax-only modeling.
